translations.text: When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven, for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
If your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you, for it is better for you to lose one of your body parts than for your whole body to fall into Gehenna.
But I tell you, do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is God's throne,
nor swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your word be 'Yes' for yes and 'No' for no, for anything more than that comes from the evil one.
But when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the assemblies and in the public squares, so that people will praise them. Truly I tell you, that is their reward.
The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eye is generous, your whole body will be full of light.
Therefore do not worry and say, 'What shall we eat?' or 'What shall we drink?' or 'What shall we wear?'
Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day's own trouble is enough.
Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
When he entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him and pleaded with him.
So that the word spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled: 'He took away our illnesses and bore our pains.'
A scribe approached and said to him, 'Teacher, I too will follow you wherever you go.'
One of his disciples said to him, 'Lord, give me permission to go first and bury my father.'
Then John's disciples approached him and said, 'Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?'
And behold, a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years approached from behind and touched the fringe of his garment.
He said to them, 'Go away, for the girl is not dead but sleeping.' And they laughed at him.
When he entered the house, the blind men approached him, and Jesus said to them, 'Do you believe that I can do this for you?' They said to him, 'Yes, Lord.'
They went out and spread the news about him throughout that whole region.
As they were going out, behold, they brought to him a mute man possessed by a demon.
But the Pharisees said, 'He casts out demons by the ruler of the demons.'
Jesus sent out these twelve, instructed them, and said, 'Do not go along a road to the Gentiles, and do not enter a city of the Samaritans,
but go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.'
Everyone who acknowledges me before people, I too will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven.
Do not think that I came to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink because he is a disciple—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
And blessed is whoever does not stumble because of me.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
The men of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching. And look, something greater than Jonah is here.
He said to them, “An enemy did this.” The servants said to him, “Do you want us to go and gather it up?”
He answered them, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.”
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid. Then, in his joy, he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
He sent and had John beheaded in prison.
Those who were in the boat came forward and worshiped him, saying, “Truly you are the Son of God.”
They worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines commandments given by human beings.
He called the crowds to him and said to them, “Listen and understand.”
Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. When a blind person leads a blind person, he goes astray, and both fall into a pit.
Jesus said, “Are you too still without understanding?”
“Do you not understand that everything that enters the mouth goes into the stomach and passes out?”
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
“Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?”
Jesus went into the region of Caesarea Philippi and asked his disciples, “Who do people say that I, the Son of Man, am?”
They said, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and some Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
Jesus answered him, “Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.”
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
They lifted their eyes and saw no one but Jesus alone.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, “Why could we not cast him out?”
And he said, “Truly I tell you, unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.”

And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a millstone turned by a donkey hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
Again I tell you, if two of you agree on earth about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
He says to them, “Because of your hardness of heart, Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so.”
And he says to them, “Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.”
When those of the eleventh hour came, they each received one denarius.
Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death.
But all this happened so that the word of the prophet might be fulfilled, who says:
Listen to another parable. There was a landowner who planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, leased it to tenant farmers, and went to a foreign country.
Now when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenant farmers?
They say to him, “He will bring those wicked men to a terrible end and lease the vineyard to other tenant farmers who will give him the fruit at the proper times.”
And whoever falls on this stone will be shattered, and anyone on whom it falls, it will crush.
Then the king says to the servants, “Bind his feet and hands and cast him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.”
When they heard this, they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
And whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.
And he answered and said to them, “Do you see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be torn down.”
Nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines, massacres, and earthquakes in various places.
Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
Afterward the other virgins also come and say, “Lord, Lord, open the door for us.”
After a long time, the master of those servants comes and settles accounts with them.
The master answered and said to him, “Wicked and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter.”
And when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he says to his disciples:
But they were saying, “Not here during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”
Judas, who was going to betray him, answered and said, “Is it I, Teacher?” He says to him, “You have said it.”
Jesus says to him, “Truly I tell you that this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
And they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. Later two false witnesses came forward.
Prophesy to us, you Christ! Who struck you?
And after a little while, those standing there came forward and said to Peter, “You certainly are one of them too, for your speech gives you away.”
And he said, “I have sinned, for I have betrayed innocent blood.” And they said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
For this reason that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
Then he released Barabbas to them, and after flogging Jesus, he handed him over to be crucified.
They stripped him and put a scarlet cloak on him.
And they wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. Kneeling before him, they mocked him and said, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
When some of those standing there heard this, they said, “He is calling Elijah.”
And immediately one of them ran, took a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
And the guards trembled with fear of him and became like dead men.
And if this reaches the judge’s ears, we will persuade him and keep you free from worry.
